headline: Revoked licenses for Hurricane Betty's at 350 Southbridge and Icy Gaming at 117 Lovell Street.
summary: Approved one-day liquor and entertainment licenses for the Holiday Market, Festival of Lights, and Museum of Worcester events, plus two common victualer licenses, a manager change, and an entertainment license expansion. At two violation hearings, police presented reports and residents spoke, and the commission voted 3-0 to revoke licenses at both businesses.
decisions: Approved one-day liquor licenses for Ashland Brewing's Worcester Holiday Market at 211 Commercial Street, 3-0.
Approved one-day entertainment license for the Festival of Lights on Worcester Common, 3-0.
Approved one-day liquor license for the City of Worcester Festival of Lights, 3-0.
Approved one-day liquor licenses for Worcester Historical Museum dba Museum of Worcester, 3-0.
Approved common victualer license for Ciro's Pizza at 186 Stafford Street, 3-0.
Approved common victualer license for Dragon Dynasty at 104 Highland Street, 3-0.
Approved change of manager for Worcester Detachment Marine Corps League at 181 Lake Avenue, 3-0.
Approved entertainment license expansion for Eddy’s Pub and Sports Bar at 120 Stafford Street, 3-0.
Revoked common victualer and entertainment licenses for Icy Gaming at 117 Lovell Street, 3-0.
Revoked liquor and entertainment licenses for Jolo, Inc. dba Hurricane Betty’s at 350 Southbridge, 3-0.

Violation Hearings 
 
9. Icy Gaming, 117 Lovell Street 
 
Sergeant Needham presented the following: 
 
On September 5, 2026, Sergeant Thomas Needham was assigned to the Alcohol Enforcement Unit 
and became aware of a call to the premises. Sergeant Needham was familiar with the premises due 
to prior incidents. Worcester Police had previously discussed with the owner activities that were 
not allowed on site, one of which was the use of tobacco/hookah on site. The business does not 
possess a hookah license. 
 
At about 12:40 a.m., Sergeant Needham and other officers arrived at the scene and observed 
approximately 35-30 individuals milling around the parking lot and sidewalk area. Officers could 
see a large crowd of people inside. 
 
While in the parking lot, Sgt. Needham could see smoke coming from the interior of the building 
as individuals entered and exited indicating smoking inside the building.  
 
Sergeant Needham spoke to the owner, Ayub Ali, and asked how many people were inside the 
premises. Mr. Ali stated that he was unsure.  
 
They both went inside. Sergeant Needham could see and smell tobacco smoke and the aroma of 
burnt marijuana smoke.
The loudspeaker was playing amplified music and the crowd inside was estimated to be over 50 
people.  
 
The business is only permitted to open to Midnight.  
 
Officers gave orders that everyone needed to leave. Once the crowd was dispersed, Sergeant 
Needham observed six still warm to touch hookah pipes, shisha tobacco, an empty bottle of 750ml 
Don Julio Tequilla, and a 1.75 liter half full bottle of Lunazul tequila.  
 
The bottles of alcohol were recovered from the trash located next to the kitchen area. The pipes 
and tobacco were located under a food service area just outside the kitchen. The business does not 
possess a liquor license. 
 
 While on site, the owner was asked where his permits were, and he stated was unable to locate but 
would have them next evening. 
 
On September 6, 2026, Sergeant Needham was monitoring the premises and could clearly see 
individuals entering the premises after Midnight. 
 
Based on his observations he requested Officer Patrick Harrington and other officers to respond 
to the location.  
 
Upon entering the premises, the owner was present, and the officers could smell smoke and the 
aroma of burnt marijuana. 
 
 Officer Harrington discovered a hookah pipe located by the side door leading to the neighboring 
business.  
 
The pipe was still warm to the touch. The owner stated he was smoking the hookah inside the 
establishment.  
 
While inside the business officers observed party decorations hanging from the ceiling and that 
the door leading to Lovell Street was covered and taped with a black trash bag over the window 
portion. The door had an illuminated Exit sign over it, but the door was deadbolted shot.  
 
Sergeant Needham again asked for the licenses for the business and again the owner could not 
produce.  
 
The owner failed to appear for the hearing. 
 
Kevin Ksen who said he lives diagonally across from location, and one evening it was a melee, with 
young people running through the area and cars quickly leaving as police arrived. 
Etel Haxhiaj, who stated that she lives near the business, called for its license to be suspended and 
said she and other residents had raised concerns about the property before the October 
inspection.
Several other neighbors spoke about the location being a nuisance for the neighbors. 
Commissioner Charran Fisher moved to revoke the license, pointing in part to the owner’s 
absence from the hearing and the severity of the allegations described by city officials. 
Commissioner Cruz called the 211-person crowd in a 16-person space outrageous. This is just 
sheer arrogance; she stated when it comes to disregarding the law and the safety of others. She 
stated that she supports small businesses, but this is completely outrageous.” 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to revoke the common victualer and entertainment 
licenses. 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated October 23, 2026. 
 
10. Jolo, Inc. dba Hurricane Betty’s, 350 Southbridge  
 
Violations of Rule #1 (2 counts), Rule #14, #17, #29, #3 
 
Sergeant Needham presented the following: 
  
October 11, 2026, the Worcester Police department responded to  Hurricane Betty’s located at 350 
Southbridge St. in response to a ShotSpotter activation that came in at 2:06 a.m.   
  
2. R esponding officers arrived on scene and found one adult male in the roadway 
suffering from multiple gunshots.    
  
3. T he victim was treated on scene and transported to UMASS Hospital -Lake Ave, 
where he received further treatment but succumbed to his injuries.    
  
4. O fficers were told that a second gunshot wound victim had been transported to 
UMASS Memorial Hospital on Belmont St. The victim was transported by a private 
vehicle and not by ambulance.   
  
5. I t was determined through investigation that the second victim was involved in the 
incident at Hurricane Betty’s and received injuries because of that incident.   
  
6. P atrol supervisors responded to the scene and requested Detective Bureau personnel 
to respond due to the nature of the incident. Officers from the Detective Bureau 
responded and began the process of their investigation.   
  
7. V ideo evidence of the interior and exterior of Hurricane Betty’s was provided to 
Detectives by employees of the business. The video evidence recovered included footage 
prior to the incident and after the incident. That video evidence was recovered and 
uploaded to Evidence.com.   
  
8. The recovered video displayed a date and timestamp indicating when the recording 
was captured. The displayed time was three hours behind the actual time (for example,
2:00 a.m. was recorded as 11:00 p.m.). The recovered video evidence covered the period 
between 1:00 a.m. and 2:30 a.m.  
  
9. S ergeant Thomas Needham, of the Worcester Police Alcohol Enforcement unit, 
viewed footage of the incident.  
  
10. S gt. Needham was able to clearly identify violations of the Rules and Regulations of 
the Worcester License Commission on the video.    
  
11. A summary of the observations from the video is as follows:   
  
a. A t 1:47 a.m., a patron walked out of the front door of the business with a clear 
plastic cup containing colored liquid. The person had the cup concealed under the 
chest portion of their jacket when exiting. Upon reaching the sidewalk, the 
individual removed the cup and stood around on the sidewalk conversing with 
other individuals.   
  
b. A t 1:49 a.m., three individuals entered the business and appeared to be advised 
by security that it was too late to enter the club. The three individuals remained 
at the entrance and eventually moved to the right of the walk -through metal 
detector and entered the club. None of the individuals passed through the metal 
detector and none of the individuals presented any identification to be scanned as 
required on the license. The three individuals ordered and were served alcoholic 
beverages.   
  
c. A t 1:52 a.m., security personnel used a set of keys on the front door, allowing 
the front door to be pushed open by patrons to leave, but also causing the front 
door to be locked to any individuals attempting to enter the business.   
  
d. A t 1:53 a.m., a patron walked out the front door of the business in possession 
of a plastic cup containing a colored liquid.   
  
e. A t 1:55 a.m., four individuals entered the business when the front door opened 
while patrons were leaving. Two individuals moved to the left of the walk-through 
metal detector and two walked through the detector where they were stopped by 
security who appe ared to tell the individuals that it was too late to enter the 
business. While advising the four individuals, security walked away from the 
entrance and towards the middle of the bar for a disturbance.  While security was 
responding to the disturbance, the front entrance was no longer manned, and four 
individuals entered the business.    
  
f. T he two individuals that had walked through the detector were not given a 
secondary frisk after the machine alerted. The other two individuals entered the 
business without walking through the detector. None of the four individuals 
presented any identification for scanning.   
  
g. A t 1:56 a.m., a patron walked out of the front door of the business with an 
open bottle of beer.
h. A t 1:57 a.m., a patron walked out of the front door of the business with a clear 
plastic cup containing a colored liquid.   
  
i. A t 1:58 a.m., a patron inside the business had a bottle of Don Julio tequila.  The 
business was not authorized to conduct “bottle service.”  
  
j. A t 2:20 a.m., a verbal confrontation between patrons who had left the business 
broke out at the front entrance to the business. One security person exited the 
doorway and attempted to separate the individuals. The verbal altercation turned 
into a physical altercation and went from pushing and shoving to throwing 
punches. Two more security personnel exited the club to assist the first security 
person. The altercation involved numerous people and moved northbound 
(towards downtown) on the sidewalk from the entrance. In addition to the three 
security personnel who were outside attempting to actively stop the physical 
fighting, a female bartender came out onto the sidewalk and observed the assault. 
A fourth security person exited the club and assisted other security personnel in 
attempting to break up the fighting.    
  
k. T he group that was actively engaged in a physical fight moved back toward 
the entrance of the business, and the fighting appeared to end. At that time, a 
patron walked out of the club carrying a full 750 ml bottle of Don Julio tequila. 
This was the same individual who had possessed the bottle inside the club earlier.  
  
l. T wo other patrons exited the business with plastic cups containing an alcoholic 
mixed drink that had been made by the bartender and served to them. These 
individuals stood on the sidewalk watching the disturbance while in possession of 
the alcoholic bevera ges. One of the individuals with a drink engaged in a 
conversation with the same bartender that had come out onto the sidewalk to 
observe the disturbance.   
  
m. A t 2:03 a.m., the group involved in the disturbance was still gathered outside 
the front door of the business. Security personnel were still on the sidewalk in the 
same area. At this time, one of the patrons involved in the initial assault 
approached a patron that was also involved in the initial disturbance/assault and 
began to strike that individual. The person had an object in their hand while they 
were striking the other individual in the head area.  Other patrons that were also 
involved in the initial assault/disturbance joined in on the assault against the 
individual being struck with the object.    
  
n. Se curity personnel that were outside on the sidewalk witnessed the assault and 
attempted to break the fight up. The group, including security, spilled out onto 
Southbridge St. and continued fighting. Members of the group involved in the 
assault on the individual reassembled on the sidewalk in front of the business. 
Security remained outside monitoring the group. The group then began to move 
northbound on the sidewalk again. When they reached the end of the front of the 
business, there appeared to be another disturbance.
o. At 2:06 a.m., patrons and security ran southbound on the sidewalk and 
appeared shocked and scared. Security personnel ran into the business by the 
front door and closed the door behind them. The timing of the group running on 
the sidewalk matched the time gunfire was detected by the ShotSpotter system.    
  
p. A t 2:07 a.m., the bartender who had been outside on the sidewalk moved back 
inside the Licensed Premises. She made a call on her cell phone. Based on the 
timeframe, it appeared that the call was to police reporting the incident.    
  
q. A t 2:08 a.m., patrol officers arrived on scene and rendered aid to a victim lying 
in the roadway. Officers arriving on scene also attempted to enter the business, 
but the unstaffed front door was locked. Officers pounded on the door and 
announced “Police” before the door was opened. The recovered video evidence 
showed security personnel inside the business, with the door closed and locked, 
looking through the door’s window during the verbal argument and both physical 
assaults.  
  
At no time did any security personnel outside attempt to notify personnel inside the club to call the 
po
lice. At no time did anyone from the business call the police department regarding the physical 
assault. The video footage showed approximately 62 patrons leaving the business. The occupancy 
permit for the Licensed Premises allowed 49 people. The number leaving did not include the four 
security personnel outside the business on the sidewalk. Another security individual appeared on 
video inside the business and was also the named manager on the license. The two bartenders, DJ, 
and numerous dancers working at the club that evening were also not included. The business was 
operating well in excess of the occupancy permitted.  
  
 The video showed that, starting at 1:00 a.m., nine patrons who entered the Licensed Premises did 
not have their IDs scanned. Six patrons entered without passing through the metal detector or 
having their IDs scanned. Four individuals passed through the me tal detector, which alerted, but 
did not receive a secondary frisk. One patron also entered, passed through the metal detector, and 
scanned their own ID. No security personnel were present at the entrance at that time. Between 1:30 
a.m. and 1:40 a.m., ten individuals entered the Licensed Premises. From 1:40 a.m. to 1:45 a.m., five 
individuals entered. From 1:45 a.m. to 2:00 a.m., eleven individuals entered. Further, between 1:46 
a.m. and 1:54 a.m., two bartenders continued to serve patrons and served more than 20 alcoholic 
beverages. 
 
Scottie Foreman along with Attorney Sean Smith appeared to answer to the violation. Attorney 
Smith stated that they did not dispute the fast as presented.  
 
Multiple family members of the victim shared their experiences regarding the impact of the 
establishment on their lives and urged the License Commission to revoke its licenses.  
 
Attorney Smith acknowledged the tragedy and confirmed that the employees of  Hurricane Betty’s  
were cooperative during the investigation and will maintain their cooperation. He mentioned that the 
establishment plans to overhaul its management and hire external security moving forward.  
 
The Commission pointed out that the Licensed Premises has a history of three previous violations, 
including another homicide that took place on the premises in 2022.
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to revoke the liquor and entertainment licenses. 
 
List of Exhibits: Police report dated October 10, 2026 
 
Adjournment 
 
Upon a roll call the Commission voted 3-0 to adjourn the meeting at 11:37 a.m.
